# Spring Retargeting

<!-- Generated by generate-swiftui-skill.py; edit the library sources. -->

Category: Motion

Send a second target before the first spring settles to compare input locking with a spring that responds immediately to new state.

- Before: New targets are blocked
- After: Springs accept new targets

APIs: `spring`, `withAnimation`, `completionCriteria`

## Complete improved example

Adapt the behavior to the app; demonstration controls and values are illustrative.

```swift
import SwiftUI

// iOS 17+. Present SpringsDoExample() in your app.
struct SpringsDoExample: View {
    @State private var phase = 0
    @State private var resetID = 0

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 20) {
            SpringsDoContent(phase: phase)
                .frame(maxWidth: 320, minHeight: 180)
                .id(resetID)
            Button("Run example") { phase += 1 }

            Button("Reset") { phase = 0; resetID += 1 }
        }
        .padding()
    }
}

struct SpringsDoContent: View {
    var font: Font = .largeTitle
    let phase: Int
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @State private var target = false

    var body: some View {
        Image(systemName: "tray.fill")
            .font(font)
            .offset(x: reduceMotion ? 0 : (target ? 45 : -45))
            .accessibilityLabel(target ? "Archive" : "Inbox")
            .onChange(of: phase) { move() }
    }

    // excerpt:start
    private func move() {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 1.2)) {
            target = !phase.isMultiple(of: 2)
        }
    }
    // excerpt:end

}
```
